sources.entry: Loop - Window management made elegant. [Freeware][Freeware Icon] [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/MrKai77/Loop)

summary.one_liner: Loop is a free, open-source macOS window manager that lets you move and resize windows using a radial menu, keyboard shortcuts, or URL-scheme commands.
summary.what_it_does: Loop is a macOS app for arranging windows. Holding a trigger key and moving the cursor opens a radial menu for choosing a window direction, which moves or resizes the active window. Users can also bind any key to work with the trigger key to run a specific action. A preview outline shows the result before it is applied. Cycles repeat actions when the same shortcut or left-click is pressed repeatedly. Stash hides windows at the screen edge and brings them back on hover or keybind. The README also lists a large set of built-in actions (halves, quarters, thirds, screen switching, growing and shrinking, undo, initial frame) and supports control through shell commands and AppleScript via a loop:// URL scheme.
use_cases: arrange windows on macOS with the keyboard
snap windows to halves, quarters, or thirds
script window layouts from shell or AppleScript
hide windows at the screen edge to reduce clutter
replace manual window dragging with a radial menu
how_to_run: Or download the latest .zip from the release page and run the app
Set a trigger key in Settings > Behavior (Right Control is suggested after remapping Caps Lock)
open "loop://direction/right" to move the active window to the right half
stack: Swift (inferred from macOS app; not named in README)
URL scheme (loop://) with shell and AppleScript control
notable: Radial menu triggered by a held key and cursor movement, with optional toggle
Live preview of the resize before it is committed
Cycles: repeat the same shortcut or click to chain window actions
Stash feature to hide windows at a screen edge
Scriptable through a loop:// URL scheme, including list commands
caveats: Caps Lock as trigger requires remapping keys in System Settings or an external app such as Hyperkey or Karabiner Elements
The README's comparison table is self-reported and may be outdated
